scope.summary: This standard prescribes the requirements, chemical formulation parameters, application methods, physical-mechanical testing limits, and sampling protocols for the material commercially known as ready mixed paint, stoving, red oxide zinc chrome, priming, used as a high-integrity anti-corrosive primer in paint systems for protecting steelwork, sheet metal, and industrial machinery under inland, marine, or industrial outdoor/indoor conditions.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Chemical Department / Paints and Varnishes)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification under the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS). However, paint manufacturers are highly encouraged to apply for a BIS license to print the prestigious BIS 'Standard Mark' (ISI Mark) directly on the paint drums and containers. This serves as a certified guarantee of anti-corrosive performance, stoving kinetics, and weather-exposure durability. Compliance with IS 2075 is strictly demanded in major engineering supply contracts, automotive and machinery fabrication tenders, railway coach paint specifications, and defense logistics across India.

requirements.detail: The paint film is formulated to be baked (stoved) to form an incredibly tough, highly cross-linked, and impervious polymer barrier. The baking schedule must be performed at temperatures ranging from 100°C to 150°C (typically 120°C) [2] for approximately 30 minutes [2, 3].
The primer must cure rapidly under heat, showing no soft, tacky, or wet films at the completion of the designated stoving period [2, 4].

The stoved primer film must show exceptional compatibility when overcoated with finishes, including synthetic stoving enamels, showing no signs of lifting, wrinkling, or blistering under subsequent baking [5-8].
After baking, the paint film must dry to a smooth, uniform, and eggshell-flat or semi-gloss finish [5-7, 9] that provides an excellent mechanical key for finishing topcoats.

The pigment must comprise a balanced mixture of high-purity red oxide (iron oxide) for physical barrier protection and zinc chrome pigment to provide active galvanic and passivating corrosion inhibition on metal substrates [4, 10, 11].
Restricts volatile solvent content to limit atmospheric VOC emissions and ensure a high solid-content density of the wet paint [9, 11, 12].
Each container must be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, brand, date of manufacture, batch number, shelf life, and the stoving schedule parameters [13, 14].

All observed or calculated test and analytical values must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained in the rounded value must match the specified limit.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 2075 : 2017 (Third Revision) is the national Indian Standard specification establishing technical, chemical, and testing requirements for stoving red oxide zinc chrome priming paint. Maintained under the paints and varnishes sectional committee (CHD 20) and reaffirmed in 2022, this standard regulates high-performance industrial primers applied to steelwork and sheet metal. Unlike air-drying primers, stoving primers are heat-cured (baked) in industrial ovens at temperatures ranging from 100°C to 150°C (commonly 120°C) for 30 minutes, forming an exceptionally tough, chemically resistant, and impervious protective layer. The standard specifies pigment compositions (combining barrier iron oxide and passivating zinc chromate), restricts volatile organic solvent content, and details performance tests—including finish texture, rapid curing speeds, and overcoat compatibility—to ensure maximum corrosion protection and durability across India's industrial, automotive, and manufacturing sectors.
